lead.title: Field-grown GM bananas carry nutritionally relevant iron and zinc, but with a yield cost
lead.summary: A New Phytologist field evaluation in Australia grew 450 genetically modified Cavendish and Lady Finger banana plants carrying six iron-homeostasis transgenes. Fruit iron and zinc reached 45.5 and 51.9 mg per kg dry weight with OsNAS expression, and 28 lines supplied at least 50% of the estimated average requirement of iron for children. Higher mineral content correlated with lower yield, partly eased by co-expressing OsVIT1. Results are from the first planting crop only and are not yet East African field data.

notes.label: Plant science
notes.text: D14 is shown to stabilise PHR1, tying strigolactone to phosphate signalling in Arabidopsis, and a peanut single-nucleus atlas of 29,308 nuclei flags AhWRKY40 for stem rot resistance.

notes.label: Biotech
notes.text: A cereal pangene atlas finds 59 to 264% more family members than single genomes, and a review urges CRISPR editing of dual-function susceptibility genes.

notes.label: Prairies
notes.text: Barley HvMAPK5-HvWRKY75-HvHKT1;2 is a salt tolerance module, and a 19-year wheat trial links salinity to crown rot, so both are relevant to saline Prairie soils (my inference, as the work was done in the lab or in China).

plant.title: Strigolactone receptor D14 integrates phosphate and strigolactone signaling by stabilizing PHR1
plant.summary: Under low phosphate, strigolactone-induced anthocyanin needs PHR1, and the strigolactone receptor D14 binds PHR1 in a strigolactone-dependent way. The interaction promotes PHR1 dimerization, blocks its ubiquitination-mediated degradation and boosts its activity, so the complex switches on strigolactone and anthocyanin biosynthesis genes. This explains why strigolactone has opposite effects on lateral roots under low and high phosphorus. The work is in Arabidopsis; peer-reviewed, abstract read.

plant.title: HvMAPK5 phosphorylates HvWRKY75 to switch on HvHKT1;2 and strengthen barley salt tolerance
plant.summary: The kinase HvMAPK5 phosphorylates the transcription factor HvWRKY75 at Ser21, which stabilises it and raises its activation of the sodium transporter gene HvHKT1;2. Overexpression of HvHKT1;2 increased sodium efflux at the root apex, cut shoot sodium and raised the K/Na ratio, while knockdown did the opposite. Peer-reviewed lab-scale work in barley, with no field yield data in the abstract.

plant.title: Single-nucleus atlas of peanut stem rot points to AhWRKY40 as a resistance regulator
plant.summary: Profiling 29,308 nuclei and 52,819 expressed genes, the study found that infection with Sclerotium rolfsii mostly downregulated genes and shrank every cell population, with epidermal cells carrying the highest share of resistance genes. Overexpressing AhWRKY40 raised resistance and increased jasmonic and salicylic acid. Peer-reviewed; transgenic validation was not described as field-scale.

plant.title: A potassium channel beta-subunit blocks potyvirus replication and movement by binding 6K2
plant.summary: Nicotiana benthamiana NbKNB1 binds the turnip mosaic virus 6K2 protein, disrupting 6K2 self-association and vesicle maturation, and competes with the viral CI protein to limit cell-to-cell movement. A mutant lacking residues 270 to 279 lost both effects, and the maize homolog ZmKZB1 also reduced infection by other potyviruses. Peer-reviewed; the core work is in N. benthamiana.

plant.title: Class I TCPs TCP14 and TCP15 restrain ABA signalling and are themselves destabilised by ABA
plant.summary: TCP14 and TCP15 activate negative regulators of ABA signalling such as AFP2, suppressing ABI5 under non-stress conditions, while ABA lowers TCP protein abundance to release the brake in stress. The loop fine-tunes the trade-off between growth and stress responses. Arabidopsis-only, peer-reviewed.

plant.title: The S-domain receptor-like kinase HIB1 controls auxin distribution and root gravitropism via MPK6
plant.summary: A forward screen identified HIB1; mutants show shorter primary roots, fewer lateral roots and weak gravitropism because of abnormal auxin distribution and PIN protein polarity. The gravitropic defect tracks with raised MPK6 activity and is rescued by loss of MPK6. Arabidopsis-only, peer-reviewed.

plant.title: An MdERF4 and MdERF106 switch drives a self-reinforcing MdWRKY33 loop behind irreversible apple softening
plant.summary: MdWRKY33 activates the cell wall gene MdPG, its own promoter and ethylene production. Ethylene represses the repressor MdERF4 and induces the activator MdERF106, locking in the softening programme. Peer-reviewed; offers candidate targets for firmness, with no storage trial reported in the abstract.

plant.title: Volatiles from salt-stressed rice trigger stress responses in unstressed neighbours
plant.summary: Salt-tolerant Pokkali under 200 mM NaCl emitted more dimethyl sulfide and limonene, and neighbouring salt-sensitive Uma showed biochemical and molecular shifts and a changed metabolome. Docking suggests limonene binds putative odorant-binding proteins. Peer-reviewed, airtight chamber lab setup, so field relevance is untested.

plant.title: Review: chromatin factors that push back against Polycomb silencing in plants
plant.summary: The review collects chromatin factors that restrict, remove or counterbalance Polycomb marks (H2AK121 monoubiquitination and H3K27me3) so that developmental transitions and environmental responses stay reversible. Review article, no new data.

plant.title: Review: plant sexual reproduction in a warming world
plant.summary: The authors propose that heat stress causes a system-level breakdown of male and female gametophyte development, shared metabolic and proteostatic support, and pollen-pistil interaction, rather than isolated organ failures. Review and conceptual framework, no new data.

biotech.title: Field-grown GM bananas reach nutritionally relevant iron and zinc, at a yield cost
biotech.summary: In an Australian field evaluation of 450 plants carrying six iron-homeostasis transgenes, fruit iron and zinc reached 45.5 and 51.9 mg per kg dry weight with OsNAS expression and higher nicotianamine. Twenty-eight lines met 50% of the estimated average requirement for children. Mineral gains correlated with lower yield, partly offset by co-expressing OsVIT1. First planting crop only; peer-reviewed.

biotech.title: Review: editing dual-function susceptibility genes for multistress-resilient crops
biotech.summary: The authors argue that susceptibility (S) genes whose loss helps both disease resistance and abiotic stress tolerance are priority CRISPR targets, and propose screening candidates in both directions. Opinion and review piece, no new experiments.

biotech.title: A pangene family atlas of four cereals shows large uncharacterised allelic diversity
biotech.summary: Across nearly 500 pangene families, pangenome-level family membership was 59 to 264% larger than single-genome counts, and many accumulation curves were far from saturation even with 320 rice genomes. Copy-number remodeling is largely hidden when only total family size is counted. Peer-reviewed computational resource.

biotech.title: Explainable AI points to recombination rate and chromatin as predictors of subgenome identity in maize
biotech.summary: Machine learning models built on 60 genomic and epigenomic features in maize ranked recombination rate as the most influential, with transposon density, chromosome position and active histone marks (H3K9ac, H3K27ac) also high. The same pattern held in a second allopolyploid. Computational and correlative, no editing validation.

biotech.title: A horizontal transposon transfer atlas across 558 plant genomes
biotech.summary: Analysing 558 genomes from 352 species, the study found 1,548 putative HTT events involving 684 transposable element families, with chromatin-related and transport-related host genes enriched near HTT regions. The framework is deliberately conservative; peer-reviewed, computational.

biotech.title: The CitRWP and CsWUS axis governs citrus regeneration with SWI/SNF chromatin remodeling
biotech.summary: CitRWP binds the CsWUS promoter and teams up with the SWI/SNF ATPase SYD to activate it, and CsWUS feeds back to repress CitRWP. CsWUS overexpression promoted somatic embryogenesis in recalcitrant callus and greatly raised in planta transformation efficiency in a model citrus, but disrupted shoot organogenesis. Peer-reviewed lab work.

biotech.title: Marker-assisted selection of ZmVTE4 haplotypes raises alpha-tocopherol in tropical maize
biotech.summary: Across 70 inbreds, amylose ranged from 14.35 to 46.07% and four ZmVTE4 lines with favourable InDel alleles had 116 to 242% more alpha-tocopherol (1.04 to 1.64 mg per 100 g). Index selection of ten genotypes predicted a 27.95% yield gain. The yield figure is a prediction, not a field result.

biotech.title: Sheath blight resistance QTLs mapped from wild rice Oryza rufipogon
biotech.summary: In backcross populations genotyped at 3,531 SNPs, 26 QTLs were found, six of them major (explaining 9.10 to 14.26% of variance), with a hotspot on chromosome 6. Pre-breeding lines with relative lesion height below 25% were identified. Peer-reviewed; pre-breeding stage.

biotech.title: GWAS of pepper fruit and yield traits finds 23 loci and 318 genes
biotech.summary: Using 195 Capsicum annuum accessions and 76,418 SNPs, the scan found 12 fruit morphology loci and 11 yield loci. Major fruit-length loci contained GA20ox1 and an OVATE family gene. Candidates need validation. Published 22 October, entered PubMed in the window.

biotech.title: Maize CBP60 family characterised: 13 genes and their stress responses
biotech.summary: The study re-identified 13 ZmCBP60 genes and examined their evolution and abiotic stress responses. Genome-wide and expression analysis only, no functional validation in the abstract I read.

ag.title: Nineteen years of salinity raise wheat crown rot; non-saline irrigation cut it by 49%
ag.summary: Severe salinity raised soil pH from 7.64 to 8.38, cut available phosphorus by 54.11% and available potassium by 37.69%, and lifted the crown rot disease index from 10.51 to 32.88 while shrinking microbial diversity. Three years of non-saline irrigation lowered the index by 49.17%. Field data from China; published 23 October.

ag.title: Straw mulching helps maize under moderate drought but much less under severe drought
ag.summary: In a two-year trial at 135, 105 and 75 mm irrigation, mulching kept growth, photosynthesis and carbon-assimilation enzymes steadier and lowered MDA and H2O2 under moderate drought. Benefits were weaker and less consistent at 75 mm. Early-growth physiology, not final yield. Published 22 October.

ag.title: New isoxazoline insecticide candidates beat fluxametamide against diamondback moth in the lab
ag.summary: Of 28 derivatives, compound Z3 had an LC50 of 0.32 ug/mL against Plutella xylostella versus 1.28 for fluxametamide, and Z2 reached 1.73 and 1.96 ug/mL against Spodoptera frugiperda and Ostrinia furnacalis. Bioassay and modelling only, early discovery stage.

ag.title: Thioester fungicide lead B22 is tenfold more potent than fenfuram against Rhizoctonia solani
ag.summary: Among 48 derivatives, B22 had an EC50 of 0.124 ug/mL (fenfuram 1.480, fluxapyroxad 0.041) and gave 79.2% protective control of rice sheath blight at 100 ug/mL in the greenhouse. Docking and an assay on porcine succinate dehydrogenase suggest SDH as the target. Early discovery, greenhouse only.

ag.title: Pyrimidinamine oxadiazole compound 6g outperforms prothioconazole on kiwifruit soft rot in vitro
ag.summary: Compound 6g had an EC50 of 7.38 ug/mL against Botryosphaeria dothidea versus 12.85 for prothioconazole, with 82.21% protective and 85.97% curative activity on kiwifruit at 200 ug/mL. Docking points to CYP51. Early discovery stage.

ag.title: SDI-YOLO11-seg tracks early cotton vigour and salt tolerance from images
ag.summary: The model reached mAP box50 of 0.961 and mask50 of 0.937 and was used to score germination, emergence, radicle length and cotyledon area in four Xinjiang varieties under six NaCl levels. Phenotyping method, controlled conditions.

ag.title: UV autofluorescence imaging spots sweet potato foot rot before symptoms appear
ag.summary: Two-band imaging at 460 and 520 nm under 375 nm excitation separated pre-symptomatic samples from controls, and scopoletin injection reproduced the pattern, consistent with phytoalexin fluorescence. It worked on a second cultivar without retuning. Exploratory descriptors, lab stage.

ag.title: New wild rice endophyte Magnaporthiopsis oryzae lifted rice yield 12.66% and cut blast disease rate 45.51% in the field
ag.summary: The fungus MB-9-27 from Oryza granulata reshaped the rice microbiome. A companion Mortierella strain raised shoot and root growth 55.8% and 51.6% and cut blast severity 18.2%. Peer-reviewed, single-study field result; trial scale not stated in the abstract.

ag.title: Festulolium yield stability across six Anatolian environments is mostly driven by environment
ag.summary: Environment explained about 96% of treatment variation for yield traits; Achillis was the highest yielding, while Perseus (ASV 22.7) and Lofa (ASV 31.8) were the most stable. GEI was significant for crude protein, ADF and NDF. Three-year irrigated trial in Turkey.

ag.title: Trichoderma harzianum A3.1 inhibits the new fig root rot pathogen Fusarium kazakhstanicum by 72.5%
ag.summary: The study reports F. kazakhstanicum as a fig root rot pathogen in China for the first time and found A3.1 inhibited mycelial growth by 72.5% in dual culture. Plate assays only, no field efficacy reported.

methods: Last issue was 2026-11-06, so the window is 6 to 7 November 2026, using PubMed entry dates; each item date is the publication date in its PubMed record. Web news searches for gene editing, company and Saskatchewan crop report items found nothing dated in the window (latest Saskatchewan figures found were for early October), so no news or company claims are included and every item comes from PubMed abstracts. Source pages were not opened, only abstracts were read. Four items were published in PubMed records on 22 to 23 October and entered PubMed in the window, and two Plant Methods and BMC items carry journal-issue dates, so their listed date is the entry date. Reviews, Arabidopsis or N. benthamiana-only, lab-stage and discovery-stage chemistry are flagged. Items already in earlier briefings were skipped.
